acceptance_rule: A phase may be accepted when every blocking question is resolved and every acceptance criterion/mapped axis is pass or not_applicable, except that an explicitly partial criterion/axis may be accepted only when it is represented by a canonical carried_release_gate naming the source criterion/axis and a concrete target phase/criterion. An open carried gate remains a blocker for final release; after the target criterion/axis passes, the carry is marked resolved while the source phase retains its historical partial status. A phase-local pass does not close the axis globally. P8 performs consolidated global review of every release-gate axis plus promoted carried gates before release.

axes.name: Purpose & Markdown-first boundary
axes.definition: Engine preserves Markdown-first documentation and only introduces structured/managed machinery where explicitly justified.

axes.name: Documentation ownership & storage layout
axes.definition: Structured data and dependency state remain documentation-owned, with mirrored _structured layout and clear separation from engine code.

axes.name: Resource identity, schema & version integrity
axes.definition: Resources, schemas, refs, versions and metadata envelopes are unambiguous, validated and evolvable.

axes.name: Path confinement & data safety
axes.definition: Reads/writes/materialization cannot escape configured roots or silently destroy canonical data.

axes.name: Raw/derived separation & provenance
axes.definition: Raw objects remain immutable; derived objects are new values with traceable provenance.

axes.name: Dependency capture & granularity correctness
axes.definition: Tracked reads and explicit rules capture the exact field/object/file/collection dependencies intended by code.

axes.name: Baseline, comparator & diff correctness
axes.definition: Only relevant dependency slices are baselined; comparisons and diffs are semantically correct and reproducible.

axes.name: Invalidation & state semantics
axes.definition: Upstream changes deterministically produce correct stale/review/build-required states without claiming semantic falsity.

axes.name: Semantic review & human/AI agency
axes.definition: The engine exposes evidence and accepts explicit review decisions; it never invents semantic verdicts.

axes.name: Builder/validator determinism & idempotency
axes.definition: Deterministic operations are reproducible, retry-safe and do not create divergent state on repeated execution.

axes.name: Materialization & derived-view parity
axes.definition: Generated views are reproducible from canonical inputs; drift is detectable; output ownership is explicit.

axes.name: CLI contract, exit codes & command boundaries
axes.definition: Commands have stable responsibilities, predictable mutations, documented exit codes and consistent human/JSON surfaces.

axes.name: AI/CI usability & machine-readable protocol
axes.definition: A new AI/CI consumer can inspect, act, validate and verify without editing internal runtime files directly.

axes.name: History, provenance, diagnostics & repairability
axes.definition: Receipts/events/reasons make changes explainable and allow diagnosis/reconciliation after failures.

axes.name: Crash, retry, concurrency & transactional integrity
axes.definition: Interrupted or concurrent operations do not leave contradictory canonical/runtime state.

axes.name: Migration & backward compatibility
axes.definition: Persisted state and project contracts are versioned and can evolve without silently invalidating prior evidence.

axes.name: Domain independence, configurability & extensibility
axes.definition: Core runtime contains no research-domain assumptions and project-specific code plugs in through explicit interfaces.

axes.name: Performance & scalability
axes.definition: Graph traversal, diffing and materialization remain practical on declared synthetic project sizes.

axes.name: Test quality & assurance
axes.definition: Unit, integration, property/fixture and end-to-end tests exercise semantics rather than only happy-path compilation.

axes.name: Release, manifest, documentation & handoff integrity
axes.definition: Package contents, docs, schemas, examples, manifests and handoff instructions agree with implemented behavior.
